title: The blow-up of the boundary has Cartier boundary and dense interior
statement:
Let $T$ be qcqs, $U\subseteq T$ a quasi-compact open, and
$\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal with
$V(\mathcal I)=T\setminus U$ (one exists by
[lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists]). Let
$b:T'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)\to T$. Then $b$ is a $U$-admissible
blow-up, the extended ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$ is invertible, so
defines an effective Cartier divisor $E\subseteq T'$, its support is
$T'\setminus b^{-1}(U)$, and $b^{-1}(U)$ is scheme-theoretically dense in
$T'$. Moreover, for every further $b^{-1}(U)$-admissible blow-up
$c:T''\to T'$, the pulled-back ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T''}$ is again
invertible with support $T''\setminus(bc)^{-1}(U)$, and $(bc)^{-1}(U)$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $T''$.

proof.text: Admissibility: the quasi-compact open immersion U.ι is quasi-compact by Scheme.Opens.quasiCompact_ι applied to hU. Rewrite the center support as the complement of U. The elementary identity Disjoint U Uᶜ supplies the disjoint_support field of IsAdmissible; the other fields are I and hI. This retains the original center definitionally, so B.I = I is reflexivity. No affine unit-ideal calculation is needed because the Lean admissibility datum records disjointness itself.

*Cartier boundary.* Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center] to the finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ on $T$: the extended ideal $\mathcal J=\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor, hence is an effective Cartier ideal ([def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]) and invertible ([def-nagata-invertible-ideal]); let $E\subseteq T'$ be the effective Cartier divisor it cuts out. Support: by [def-nagata-extended-ideal], over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq b^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ with $I=\mathcal I(\operatorname{Spec}A)$, the ideal $\mathcal J$ is $IB$, and a prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ contains $IB$ if and only if its contraction to $A$ contains $I$. Hence $|E|=b^{-1}(V(\mathcal I))=b^{-1}(T\setminus U)=T'\setminus b^{-1}(U)$.

*Density.* Apply [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-nowhere-dense] to the effective Cartier divisor $E$ of step 2 on $T'$: the open complement $j\colon T'\setminus E\hookrightarrow T'$ is scheme-theoretically dense in the sense of [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open], i.e. $\mathcal O_{T'}\to j_*\mathcal O_{T'\setminus E}$ is injective (locally this is the blueprint's chart argument: on $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $E=V(a)$, $a$ a non-zero-divisor, the restriction is $B\to B_a$, injective; Stacks 07ZU, divisors.tex lemma-complement-effective-Cartier-divisor). By step 2, $T'\setminus E=b^{-1}(U)$, so $b^{-1}(U)$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $T'$.

*Persistence.* Let $c\colon T''\to T'$ be a $b^{-1}(U)$-admissible blow-up; by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup] it is identified over $T'$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(T')\to T'$ for a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K$, so it is a blow-up of $T'$. The ideal $\mathcal J=\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$ is effective Cartier by step 2, so [lemma-nagata-cartier-total-transform-blowup] makes $\mathcal J\mathcal O_{T''}$ effective Cartier and invertible. By [def-nagata-extended-ideal], $\mathcal J\mathcal O_{T''}=\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T''}$ (pullback along $bc$): on affine patches $A\to B\to C$ both are $IC=(IB)C$. The prime-contraction computation of step 2, applied to $c$ and $\mathcal J$, gives $V(\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T''})=c^{-1}(|E|)=c^{-1}(T'\setminus b^{-1}(U))=T''\setminus(bc)^{-1}(U)$. Finally [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-nowhere-dense], applied to the effective Cartier divisor cut out by $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T''}$, shows that its complement $(bc)^{-1}(U)$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $T''$ ([def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]).
